title: Taman Ismail Marzuki
description: Taman Ismail Marzuki (TIM) is Jakarta’s premier arts and cultural complex located in Central Jakarta. For film production, the complex offers highly versatile environments ranging from intimate gallery spaces to dramatic performance halls and architecturally striking exteriors, suitable for arthouse cinema, cultural documentaries, contemporary dramas, and creative industry campaigns.

The area represents the contemporary face of Jakarta, combining monumental public space with dense metropolitan activity. For film production, Bundaran HI delivers polished cinematic visuals including wide boulevards, high-rise architecture, dramatic night lighting, and dynamic traffic movement—ideal for action films, luxury commercials, urban dramas, and productions portraying modern Southeast Asian city life.

title: Pasar Glodok
description: Glodok is Jakarta’s historic Chinatown district and one of the city’s most visually distinctive urban environments. Developed from the colonial-era Chinese settlement zone after the 1740 Batavia Massacre, the area blends Chinese-Indonesian heritage with dense commercial activity. Streets are lined with temples, electronics shops, herbal medicine stores, noodle stalls, and old shophouses layered with colorful signage. The district’s narrow corridors, multicultural textures, and vibrant street life create exceptional visual depth. For film production, Glodok offers an authentic Chinatown setting ideal for period films, urban thrillers, historical narratives, social realism, and productions exploring multicultural Southeast Asian city life.

title: Kota Tua

Centered around Fatahillah Square, the district includes museums, old trading warehouses, cobblestone streets, cafés, and heritage buildings reflecting Jakarta’s maritime trading history. The area offers one of the richest historical urban environments in Indonesia. For film production, Jakarta Old Town provides cinematic European colonial aesthetics within Southeast Asia, making it highly suitable for historical dramas, period productions, fashion editorials, tourism campaigns, and large-scale scenes requiring preserved heritage architecture and atmospheric public spaces.
